reviews.one_line_contribution: A single-node measurement of how toggling vLLM prefix caching re-orders the accuracy-vs-GPU-second frontier of three experience-prefix routes (compiled static, whole bank in context, top-k retrieval) for an ALFWorld agent, plus a three-term regression that turns the measured GPU-seconds into a portable token-level accounting.
reviews.closest_prior_work: VERIFIED: arXiv:2607.12161, 'Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction' (2026-07-13, s2 lookup, cit 1). Its thesis is the proposal's thesis: context-reduction interventions (retrieval rankers, compressors, API proxies) are evaluated by tokens removed, but the right unit is cost per successful task including cache behavior and trajectory change, and token reduction is not a reliable proxy for cost reduction in tool-heavy agents. It establishes exactly the claim the abstract opens with ('counting injected tokens is not what a serving stack charges') on a pre-specified, hash-frozen, paired campaign of 2,848 billed agent runs across 103 tasks — a larger and better-powered version of this proposal's methodological point. It does not settle the specific arm contrast here (whole bank in context vs top-k retrieval of expert trajectories, cache on vs cache off, self-hosted GPU-seconds rather than provider billing), so it is not a collision on the headline number; but it removes the framing novelty, which is most of what this proposal is selling. Second threat, also verified: arXiv:2604.05404 'Beyond Accuracy: Unveiling Inefficiency Patterns in Tool-Integrated Reasoning' (ACL, cit 4), which introduces Prefill Token Equivalents, a hardware-aware cost metric built precisely on non-reusable KV-cache accounting, i.e. the proposal's three-term model with the same motivation and already published. Third, arXiv:2606.06448 'Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications' (cit 4) is a systems characterization of agent-memory workloads that derives recommendations about amortizing construction cost via query volume — adjacent, and it will be cited against the 'nobody has measured this inside an agent loop' assertion. Not verified: the proposal's central anchor 2603.04814 — see preprint_collision.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline prediction is a systems tautology dressed as a finding, and the number it produces is not portable. P1 says an 11k shared prefix costs >=3x a 430-token per-episode prefix with caching off and <=1.5x with caching on: the direction is what prefix caching is defined to do, and the only open content is which side of a 1.5x/2x threshold the cache-on cell lands, a threshold that the proposal's own cost statistic can be moved across by tuning. GPU-seconds per episode is defined as 2 x wall-clock / episodes 'at saturated queue', with workers raised per arm until the running queue is at least 8. That is a floor, not a matched operating point: the whole-bank-80 arm's 11k KV footprint saturates at a lower concurrency than k=3, so P1 and P2 compare each arm at its own tuned concurrency, and 'the ratio' is a property of the tuning policy plus this node's 80GB KV budget as much as of the routes. The proposal concedes the fitted coefficients are not portable and that eviction behaviour is node-specific, which leaves the paper with: on one node, one 32B reader, one six-template benchmark, prefix caching worked. Second, and worse for the topic the brief is asking about: the paper's own predicted outcome makes the cost axis decision-irrelevant. If P2 holds (retrieval within 25% of static under caching) and P3/P4 hold (whole-bank matches retrieval, small banks match the full bank), then the already-measured accuracy result (k3 - static3 = +17.2 net) decides the deployment question by itself and nothing in E2-E4 changes any choice. A paper whose confirmatory result removes its own axis from the decision is a reject at ICLR main track, whatever the engineering quality.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Make the cost axis carry a decision, and make the measurement about something other than this node. (1) Replace the tuned-per-arm throughput statistic with a matched-concurrency protocol: report GPU-s per episode for every arm at the same worker count, and separately report each arm's own saturating concurrency, so the ratio and the KV-occupancy effect are two reported quantities rather than one confounded one; run the 8/16/32 ladder on all arms, not two. (2) Move the claim to where the routes actually cross. The interesting, non-tautological question is the bank-size/item-length regime at which the cached whole-bank arm stops being cheap — i.e. sweep item length (140 tokens on ALFWorld up to synthetic 1k-token items) and bank size until the cache-on ratio crosses 1, and predict that crossing from the token-level model rather than only fitting it. That is a claim other stacks can check. (3) Fix the held-out test: P5's whole-bank-24 is an interpolation point bracketed in every regressor by fitted arms, so 25% error is near-impossible; use leave-one-arm-out across all nine arms and both cache settings and report worst-case error, or fit without whole-bank-80 and extrapolate to it. (4) Drop P4's cache-hit branch, which a type-stratified 24-item bank with canonical-id ordering makes true by construction (C(4,3)=4 sets per type), and replace it with a manipulated prefix-diversity ladder: hold bank size fixed and vary the number of distinct emitted prefixes (score order vs canonical order, k=3 vs k=7, per-episode jitter) to measure the diversity elasticity of cost, which is the actual mechanism claimed in the hypothesis. (5) Add the length-matched cached placebo (below) so P1 separates length from content. (6) Re-anchor the related work on IDs that resolve, and engage 2607.12161 and 2604.05404 head-on rather than claiming the framing is new.
reviews.missing_baseline: A length-matched cached placebo prefix on the cost arms: an ~11k-token static prefix that is not the bank (padded procedures, or 80 wrong-type/shuffled-content items) run under both cache settings and both concurrency ladders. Without it, P1's cache-on ratio conflates 'a long cached prefix is cheap' with 'the whole bank is cheap', and the paper cannot say whether the decode x context-length term or the content is doing the work — the brief's own Appendix B demands token- and rate-matched placebos, and the only placebo in the design (blind1) is a 140-token accuracy control that never enters E2. A close second, also omitted: a matched-concurrency operating point for every arm (the plan tunes workers per arm, so no two cost cells are measured at the same batch composition), and the retriever's own cost (BM25 index query plus prompt assembly, and the GPU cost of the embedding retriever any real deployment would use instead of BM25) is excluded from GPU-seconds entirely, which biases every ratio in retrieval's favour.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the exact headline (a cache-toggle cost reversal between whole-bank and retrieved experience prefixes measured inside an agent loop with paired task accuracy) — but the proposal's Preprint Collision Check is credible on the systems axis and materially wrong on its own anchor. Queries I ran, all through the literature command (s2+hf; WebSearch unavailable this session, so no channel-b query was possible): (1) 'prefix caching changes accuracy cost tradeoff retrieval versus long context agent GPU seconds' --recent -> CachedSearch 2607.23159, SeKV 2606.31145, UltraQuant 2606.20474, LongSeeker 2605.05191, POLAR 2604.16583, APE 2502.05431 — all serving/compression, none pairs cache state with task accuracy across prefix routes. (2) 'accuracy versus serving cost frontier retrieved demonstrations versus all demonstrations in context prompt caching' (no recency) -> TokenPilot 2606.17016, PANDO 2605.24785, Beyond Accuracy/PTE 2604.05404, IC-Cache 2501.12689, DynaICL 2305.11170 — 2604.05404 is a hit on the cost-metric idea. (3) 'memory system versus long context break-even cost prompt caching agent turns' --recent -> Harness the Memory 2608.15008, MemOps 2607.12893, HYPIC 2607.01299, Agent Memory characterization 2606.06448, LongMemEval-V2 2605.12493 — 2606.06448 is a hit on 'cost distribution across agent-memory designs'. (4) 'RAG versus long context cost per query with and without KV cache reuse accuracy pareto' --recent -> CoinRAG 2608.07458, ProphetKV 2602.02579, Cache-Craft 2502.15734, 2604.05012 — RAG KV-reuse systems, no task-accuracy Pareto per cache setting. (5) home-vocabulary query with no agent/memory words, 'in-context example selection increases prefill cost shared prompt reuse latency throughput tradeoff' -> BatchLLM 2412.03594, LAPS 2601.11589, prompt-compression-in-the-wild 2604.02985, DynaICL 2305.11170 — nothing that scores example-selection routes on serving cost with accuracy. Verified by paper lookup: 2607.12161, 2604.05404, 2606.06448, 2607.27090 (InferScale), 2607.26497 (BM25 Wins at Scale), 2605.13880 (PREPING), 2604.02596, 2506.04301, 2607.01299 (HYPIC). COULD NOT VERIFY: 2603.04814 returned 'not found on S2 or HF'. That is the single most load-bearing citation in both the proposal's Related Work and the brief ('the one memory-vs-long-context cost study with prompt caching', 'cost is modelled per turn, never measured inside an agent loop'), and the whole novelty argument rests on characterising it as modelled-not-measured. An unresolvable anchor means the gap it defines is unestablished; the proposal must either fix the id or drop the claim. I also did not attempt s2:62b577ec (AdaptiveScale). Finally, the check as written scores its own novelty on absence — 'no paper measures a cache-toggle cost reversal' — while missing 2607.12161, which was returned by the automated novelty card at sim 0.59 and makes the proposal's framing claim on a larger paired campaign; a collision check that does not engage the top-ranked card entry it was handed is thin.
